title: Final agentic RAG merge-policy experiment
researchQuestion: Can language-balanced evidence accumulation across attempts recover complementary comparative evidence that the current replacement policy discards, without harming abstention or general retrieval quality?
hypothesis: For explicit two-technology comparisons, retaining up to two highest-scoring chunks per requested technology across both attempts will recover at least one previously failed comparison while preserving the semantic gate's zero false-positive rate.
singleChangedVariable: Cross-attempt evidence merge policy: replace the previous attempt versus accumulate and apply a per-requested-technology quota.

variants.description: Only the current attempt's top four chunks are assessed.

Deduplicate all chunks seen so far; for explicit multi-technology questions reserve floor(topK / requested technologies) positions per technology, then fill remaining positions by cosine score. For zero or one detected technology, retain ordinary global score ordering.

frozenControls.semanticAssessor: openai/gpt-5.4-mini, medium reasoning, prompt and schema v2
frozenControls.planner: gemini-3.5-flash, low reasoning, 512 output tokens, one controlled format recovery

candidateMergePolicy.input: deduplicated union of chunks retrieved in attempts one and two
candidateMergePolicy.technologyDetection: existing detectQueryMetadataConstraint on the original question
candidateMergePolicy.quota: floor(topK / number of requested database languages) per requested language
candidateMergePolicy.withinLanguageOrdering: descending cosine score, then prior rank, then chunk id
candidateMergePolicy.remainingCapacity: highest-scoring unselected chunks regardless of language
candidateMergePolicy.output: exactly min(topK, available unique chunks) chunks reranked from one
candidateMergePolicy.nonComparativeBehavior: ordinary global mergeRankings over accumulated chunks
candidateMergePolicy.defaultRuntimeBehavior: unchanged; accumulation is opt-in for this experiment

diagnostics: attempt-one, attempt-two, cumulative, and selected chunk ids
semantic decisions before and after accumulation
provider calls, cache hits, tokens, cost, and latency

selectionRule.decision: Advance only to a separately preregistered generation-quality experiment if every requirement passes. If any requirement fails, stop further Agentic RAG development for the current thesis and retain the single-pass baseline.

executionOrder: Commit this protocol before code changes.
Add an opt-in cross-attempt accumulation dependency while leaving default replacement behavior unchanged.
Test default replacement, balanced accumulation, deduplication, quota filling, non-comparative fallback, and final abstention.
Run one provider-free plan and one cache-preserving validation execution.
Publish all results and stop this research direction if any frozen check fails.

executionOutcome.decision: Stop Agentic RAG development for the current thesis and retain the single-pass baseline. Accumulation recovered three semantically useful comparisons, but canonical both-evidence coverage remained 0.25, side recall reached only 0.50, and one focused negative became a false positive. The added recall-safety tradeoff fails the frozen rule.

limitations: The motivating C/C++ trace and all validation comparators are already inspected, so this is a final targeted engineering experiment rather than independent confirmation.
Canonical chunk metrics may undervalue semantically valid alternative evidence.
Only explicit technologies recognized by the existing metadata detector receive quotas.
